title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Paralegal - Family

title: Credit Controller
description:
Role Overview
As Credit Controller you will play an important role within the credit control department in meeting cash flow requirements with a strong emphasis on building and maintaining client relationships ensuring service standards are of the highest level.

Essential Duties:
- Opening new accounts and responsible for the day-to-day management of your customer base.
- Establish and maintain internal and external customer relationships at all levels in a calm and professional manner.
- Ensure as necessary all calls, letters, statements and follow up actions are carried out in order to bring the matter to the customer's attention to obtain payment of due/overdue depts.
- Ensure the timely and pro-active co-ordination of payments in relation to cash collection and aged debt reduction.
- Resolving queries both internally and externally around outstanding invoices.
- Agree, negotiate, and enforce re-payment plans.
- Liaise directly with the Credit Control Manager to escalate issues with payment for 3rd party collection agencies.
- Maintain customer records notifying the relevant department of changes required and logging and dealing with queries.
- Managing credit limits in-line with relevant authorisations and escalate where required to the Credit Control Manager.
- Ensuring processes are followed as part of the collection requirements, account reconciliation and payments.
- Have a flexible approach to an ever-changing workload with the ability to prioritise.
- These duties are not exhaustive and may vary from time to time, depending on the needs of the business.

Skills & Qualifications:
- Minimum of 3 years' experience working in a credit control/cash collection role and ideally in a sales driven environment. MICM preferred but not essential.
- Competent with Microsoft Office products especially Excel and experience of using finance systems (IBCOS).
- Have an excellent telephone manner.
- Team player with proactive positive attitude and strong organisational skills.
- A systematic approach and an eye for detail.
- Ability to influence, negotiate and make judgements on need for consultation and escalation.

Benefits
- Company pension scheme.
- Company sick scheme.
- 24 days holiday plus bank holidays.
- Day off for your birthday.
- Life insurance x 3 salary.
- Tailored career path.
- Manufacturer training.

- Working closely with internal departments to resolve account queries and improve collection times
- Supporting the Management Accountant with month-end processes as your experience within the role develops
- Assisting with maintaining the fixed asset register, depreciation and posting month-end journals
- Supporting sales reporting, analysis and other wider finance activities

- Current or previous experience within a Credit Controller, Credit Control Assistant, Accounts Receivable, Debt Collection, Finance Assistant or similar role
- Confident managing outstanding debt and communicating with customers by telephone and email
- Strong communication skills with the ability to have challenging conversations professionally and diplomatically
- Experience allocating customer payments and maintaining accurate account records
- Experience handling and resolving invoice or payment queries
- Previous exposure to credit checks, credit limits or credit insurance would be advantageous, but is not essential
- A genuine interest in developing broader accounting and finance experience beyond Credit Control

title: Credit Controller
description:
We are working with a North Yorkshire business that is seeking a motivated Credit Controller looking to expand their financial skill set. The initial focus is managing aged debt and ensuring healthy cash flow. As you master the credit control function, you will be systematically cross-trained in broader accounting duties, including month-end support, giving you a clear pathway to a well-rounded finance career.

- Experience in a credit control, debt collection or finance admin role
- Proactive, with good problem-solving skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication, with the confidence to handle difficult conversations firmly but politely to retain strong customer relationships
- Ability to manage a varied and demanding workload with close attention to detail and accuracy

We are looking for an experienced Legal Assistant to join our Litigation team, providing high-quality administrative and legal support to Fee Earners and helping to ensure that client matters are progressed efficiently and professionally.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide comprehensive administrative and legal support to Fee Earners within the Litigation team
- Manage and progress client matters accurately and efficiently using the firm's case management system
- Open, organise, maintain and archive legal files and supporting documentation
- Assist with the preparation and organisation of legal correspondence and documentation
- Prepare letters and other client correspondence using audio typing, word processing and digital dictation
- Manage Fee Earners' diaries, including arranging client appointments, meetings and other commitments
- Deal professionally and efficiently with incoming telephone calls, client enquiries and third-party communications
- Monitor and manage incoming emails, post, photocopying and general administrative tasks
- Prepare court documentation, including electronic bundles and other documents required for hearings
- Assist with the preparation of client bills and maintain accurate account ledgers
- Ensure all work is completed in accordance with internal procedures, professional standards and regulatory requirements
- Maintain confidentiality and security of all client and firm information
- Provide support to other Legal Assistants, Fee Earners and the wider management team when required

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience working as a Legal Assistant, Legal Secretary or similar role within a Litigation department
- Good understanding of legal terminology and litigation processes
- Strong administrative and organisational skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Confident verbal and written communication skills
- A professional, approachable and client-focused manner
- The ability to prioritise workloads and manage competing deadlines
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office
- Experience using a legal case management system would be advantageous
- Experience with audio typing or digital dictation would be beneficial
- The ability to work independently while also contributing positively to a wider team

Should you have any questions or wish to apply please do not hesitate to contact Clear Legal and Financial.

Please Note: Due to the number of applications we receive we may be unable to respond to every application directly.

title: Administration assistant
description: Posterngate surgery are recruiting an efficient administration assistant to join our small team of data administrators who maintain our patient medical records with relevant clinical information with accuracy and in a timely manner to inform patient care. (Previous applicants need not apply) The data administration team contribute in maintaining accurate medical records, which includes summarising and read coding relevant information on to patients records from hospital correspondence and other sources into the practice computer system, working strictly in accordance with the practice protocols. The main responsibilities of the post-holder will be to scan documents, summarise and read code relevant information from the patients clinical records, hospital correspondence and other sources into the patients electronic SystmOne record held on the Practice Computer. Working strictly in accordance with the Practice notes summarising and read code protocols. Key Tasks Translate clinical information into appropriate read codes, forwarding letters onto GPs for checking. Summarise records and produce an accurate summary of patient medical history. Record incoming & outgoing medical records onto SystmOne from Primary Care Support England. Liaise with Primary Care Support England with any queries relating to patient records and protocols. Extraction of necessary data from clinical correspondence and input into electronic patient record. View and disseminate hospital correspondence to GPs, ensuring that any urgent actions are flagged with appropriate member of staff. Process links for pathology, radiology and microbiology results. Maintain efficient system to file historical paper medical records. Scan copies of relevant electronic and paper patient communications using SystmOne into patient records. Undertake GP2GP transactions for transfer of patient medical records. Locate and retrieve documents as needed by clinical and non-clinical staff. Prepare monthly audit reports for clinicians when requested. Process tasks, emails and general queries. Deal with patient queries.

title: Patient Services Advisor (Receptionist)
location: York, YO32 2LL, York, YO24 3BU, Huntington, YO32 9RU, York, YO32 4AG, York, YO26 6EQ
description: PREVIOUS APPLICANTS NEED NOT APPLY. -- Please note interviews for this position will be held on Thursday 05 November 2026 -- Are you looking for a more fulfilling career? One that gives you a sense of achievement knowing that each day you are helping people access the healthcare that they need? If this sounds like you, we have the perfect opportunity for you! We are looking for individuals who to join our Patient Services Team who: Are enthusiastic and self-motivated Are able to use their initiative Excellent communicators, both written and verbal Are able to listen and empathise Are keen to learn and develop Demonstrate attention to detail Can be flexible and adaptable Are competent with IT In the role of Patient Services Advisor, you will receive, assist, and direct patients in accessing the appropriate services or healthcare professionals in a courteous, efficient, and effective way whether this be face to face or over the telephone. You will also undertake a variety of administrative tasks to assist with the smooth running of the practice. In return you will receive: Full induction and training plan Named direct Line Manager Long service rewards Generous holiday entitlement Wellbeing health plan Staff wellbeing group Ride to work scheme Uniform allowance Refreshments Support to develop your skills and career Duties and Responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the General Manager, dependent on current and evolving workload and staffing levels: Opening up/locking-up of Practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with Practice protocols. Maintaining and monitoring the Practice appointments system. Processing personal requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring patients are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional. Answer internal and external telephone calls when required. Participate in evening and Saturday morning working as per the standard rota. Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail. Taking messages and passing on information. Filing and retrieving paperwork. Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with Practice guidelines. Assist the Team Leader with routine site maintenance and Health and Safety. Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with Practice procedures. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare agencies and providers. Clear and re-stock consulting rooms as required. Dealing with samples. Providing clerical assistance to Practice and Trust staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning. Ordering, re-ordering and monitoring of stationery and other supplies. Dealing with clinical waste. Provision of refreshments for staff and visitors as required; loading and emptying the dishwasher and keeping the kitchen area clean and tidy. Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter. Helping to maintain hygiene control measures. Dealing with the front-desk administration and cash handling required for non-NHS work such as patients private insurance and medical reports.

title: Clinical Team Administrator

description: An opportunity has arisen to recruit a highly motivated and experienced individual to a Clinical Team Administrator position working 18.75 hours per week supporting the CAMHS Eating disorder service. Days/hours of work will be 9am- 5pm Monday and Tuesday and 9am- 12.45pm on Wednesdays. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. The Team Administrator role is pivotal in the day-to-day operations of the multidisciplinary teams. As part of this role, you will work closely with the Clinical Lead, Clinicians, Manager, medical secretary's and the wider team to provide the best possible care to the service user. We are looking for someone who is able to multitask in a busy environment, communicate confidently and compassionately, prioritise their workload and meet deadlines, build strong working relationships with a variety of people and excellent typing skills. Experience of taking meeting minutes, using excel spreadsheets, and IT systems is essential. Please refer to the attached job description and person specification for further detailed information to ensure that you meet the role criteria before applying. This job advert may close early if a high volume of applications have been received. If interested, please apply for this post as soon as possible.

title: Patient Services Administrator
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic and reliable person, to work within our Patient Services Department. The role includes administration of correspondence relating to patients and the safe and efficient processing of data, the management of call and recall processes and other administrative tasks relating to patient care. The applicant will be able to work under their own initiative and be able to contribute to the overall work of the practice team. Previous experience in a similar role is desirable, but not essential, as training will be given. This is a full time position (37.5 hours). Salary is dependent on experience and scope to include additional responsibilities may be available. The following are the core responsibilities of the Patient Services Administrator. Processing incoming and outgoing correspondence and ensuring patient related documents are attached to the correct patient record. Processing requests for information from third parties such as insurers and solicitors Coding documents accurately onto healthcare records, identifying key information from patient correspondence. Allocation of electronic test results, taking appropriate action and informing patients and taking calls regarding test results. Making patient appointments as requested for: On the day urgent appointments following triage, Flu/Covid clinics and follow-up appointments from tasks, letters and results. Following procedure and completing required administrative protocol for any deaths Support the clinical staff with general administrative tasks as require. Summarising of patient notes for online registrations. To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of administrative duties and the provision of administrative support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include, but are not limited to, the processing of information (electronic and hard copy) in a timely manner, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers in accordance with current policies. Generic Responsibilities All staff at Filey Surgery have a duty to conform to the following, further information can be found in the attached job description: Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Safety, Health, Environment and Fire (SHELF) Confidentiality Quality and Continuous Improvement Learning and Development Collaborative Working Managing Information Service Delivery Security Professional Conduct Primary Key Responsibilities Incoming Correspondence: Process incoming and outgoing mail Scanning of patient related documentation and attaching scanned documents to patients healthcare records. Allocation of electronic letters to appropriate clinician/department (bearing in mind absences from the practice due to working days, holidays and sickness), via SystemOne workflow. Managing this correspondence with coding and completion where appropriate. Input data into the patients healthcare records as necessary Processing requests for information i.e., SAR, insurance/solicitors letters and DVLA forms Coding & Actions on documents: Identifying relevant clinical information contained in patient correspondence and input appropriate clinical codes on SystmOne Assisting with the onward management and administration of actions added by clinicians and other staff members. Data Quality and Recall Management Action patient recalls as appropriate in a timely manner Management of patient invites for NHS vaccination and immunisation programmes Carrying out system searches as required Review and manage systems for assuring compliance with Quality Outcomes Framework (QOF) Electronic Results: Allocation of electronic results received to appropriate clinician (bearing in mind absences from the practice due to working days, holidays and sickness), via SystmOne workflow. Taking appropriate action on electronic results. Informing patients and taking phone calls regarding test results Appointments: Making patients appointments as requested for: On the day (urgent) appointments (after requests have been triaged) Flu/Covid Clinics Follow-up appointments from actions on letters & results Other administrative duties : Summarising of patient notes for online registrations Following procedure and completing required administrative work for any deaths Liaising with bereaved relatives, undertakers and secondary care regarding deaths and appropriate paperwork File and store records as required Photocopy documentation as required Support all clinical staff with general administrative tasks as requested Produce and record invoices for private work and ensure records are completed when payment received Managing all enquiries in an effective manner
